clue.text: Body of writings in an Oxford or Cambridge college

definitions.meaning: a collected body of texts, such as all the works of one author
... Christi is the name of a college at both Oxford and Cambridge, usually shortened in speech

explanation.surface: Someone's collected writings are kept at an ancient university college.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected set of texts is called by the Latin word for body; both universities have a Corpus Christi college.

clue.text: What's sung by full chorus or a threesome? Nothing in it

indicators.note: the word 'in' with 'it' (the threesome) says nothing goes inside the trio

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
zero, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a piece is for a full choir or three singers, with no one singing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts O inside TRIO, the 'it' pointing back to the threesome; OR and A come straight from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A large choral work, often sacred, performed by soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

clue.text: Fruit over the sea-an apple

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Fruit shipped across the ocean turns out to be an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts PEAR above MAIN. The main for the high sea is a literary usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearmain is a long-established English variety of dessert apple.

clue.text: Like football odds on Henry holding Williams

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins

indicators.note: Henry holding the other name means it goes inside the short form of Henry

parts.note: Hal is the familiar short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Eric is the first name of a famous Williams, e.g. Eric Williams, first Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a footballer called Henry, with a teammate named Williams in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts ERIC inside HAL. SP, the starting price, is a horse-racing term for odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A football is ball-shaped, round in every direction, the way a globe is.

clue.text: Express worker is lying

parts.note: to couch something is to express it in words, as in 'couched in polite terms'
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A fast train employee is caught telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' reads as a train or courier but is the verb meaning put into words. The definition is the heraldic sense of lying.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a beast shown lying down with its head raised is described by this French-derived term.

clue.text: Relations en route for the south, east

definitions.text: Relations en route for the south, east

parts.words: Relations en route for the south, east
parts.note: relations are stories told, here by pilgrims travelling to a cathedral city in south-east England

explanation.surface: Family members heading off on a journey to the south-east of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives; it means accounts or narrations, the stories Chaucer's pilgrims tell on the road to a Kentish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's poem is a set of stories told by pilgrims riding to the shrine of Thomas Becket in Kent.

clue.text: Many on a Yorkshire river binge

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
the Ouse flows through York; on maps it is labelled R. Ouse, R for river

explanation.surface: Lots of people out on a river in Yorkshire, drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the river of York; the setter takes 'Yorkshire river' as R plus OUSE, as a map would label it.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily, a drinking spree.

clue.text: Award of honour to colonel captured by a Kentish rebel

indicators.note: the officer being captured by the rebel means it goes inside his name

parts.note: Jack Cade led the Kent rebellion of 1450 against Henry VI

explanation.surface: A medal for a colonel, who had been taken prisoner by an insurgent from Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' puts COL inside CADE, after A. Jack Cade is a figure of English history, leader of a 15th-century revolt in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade was originally the touch of a sword in conferring knighthood, now any mark of praise.

clue.text: Go and fish in the old way

parts.note: a go, as in 'your go', is a turn
the pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An invitation to go fishing in traditional fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the old way' looks like an adverb about method; 'the old way' is a noun, a road of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike was a toll road of the 18th and 19th centuries, a historic highway.

clue.text: French revolutionary coming to honourable end in the long run

indicators.note: one piece coming to another means it is followed by it

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution, killed in his bath
Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable, a courtesy title

explanation.surface: A revolutionary in France eventually meets an honourable death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' and 'in' are link words; the surface suggests Marat's violent death and the phrase 'in the long run'.
explanation.definitionFit: A race of about 26 miles is the longest standard running event.

clue.text: Tradesman sounds comparatively bloated

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: grosser means fatter or more bloated than another

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper sounds fatter than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household goods.

clue.text: Force to receive thousands in trade

indicators.note: the verb taking something in means the other letters go inside

parts.note: to coerce is to force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two give thousands

explanation.surface: Coercion used to gain thousands through business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts MM inside COERCE; the trailing 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is buying and selling, business activity on a large scale.

clue.text: Coarse material makes us belch round there in France

indicators.note: the belching word goes round the French word

parts.note: to burp is to belch
la is French for there

explanation.surface: Rough fabric makes the wearer belch, there in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts LA inside BURP. 'là' with an accent is French for there.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse fabric woven from jute or hemp, the stuff of sacking.

clue.text: In the island note how to increase the bird population

parts.note: taken as written
Cuba is a Caribbean island
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Advice on boosting the number of birds on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how to' and 'the' are link words; the definition describes what a sitting bird does to its eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep eggs warm until they hatch, which adds chicks to the flock.

clue.text: Fruit from a green tin perhaps

indicators.note: the word signals these letters could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: Fruit taken from a tinned can, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A GREEN TIN, and a tangerine might indeed come in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit, like a mandarin.

clue.text: Low point of a heavenly body

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The lowest point reached by a star or planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low point' reads as a nadir; 'Low' is a cow's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural satellite of Earth, the most familiar body in the night sky.

clue.text: If clueless, one might be trapped in this monster's lair

definitions.text: If clueless, one might be trapped in this monster's lair

parts.words: If clueless, one might be trapped in this monster's lair
parts.note: a clue (old spelling clew) is a ball of thread; without one you could not find your way out of the labyrinth in Crete

explanation.surface: A warning to the crossword solver who has no clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Theseus escaped the labyrinth by following Ariadne's thread, a 'clew', the origin of the word 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed creature of Greek myth lived at the centre of King Minos's labyrinth.

clue.text: Surpass, though being far from in form

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a school form is a class

explanation.surface: Beating someone even when well out of form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though being' links; 'form' is a school year group, not fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat decisively, by being of a much higher standard.

clue.text: Bugle heard by Adam

indicators.note: signals a word said aloud

parts.note: a bugle is a tube-shaped glass bead sewn on clothes

explanation.surface: A bugle call heard by a man called Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Adam' means the word that follows Adam: George Eliot's novel Adam Bede. 'Bugle' looks like the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's novel and its carpenter hero bear the full name Adam Bede, so this word goes by the first name.

clue.text: Debated maybe about second support for one retired

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the single letter
signals that the word could be another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A debate about whether to second support for a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges DEBATED into BEDTEAD, and 'about' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame of a bed supports someone who has gone to bed, retired for the night.

clue.text: You are said to be imprisoned by party head — stern, grim, character

indicators.note: being imprisoned means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a do is a party
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

indicators.note: signals the words are heard as letters

parts.note: you are, said aloud, sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Telling someone they are locked up by a party leader, a stern grim character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned by' puts UR (the sound of 'you are') inside DO + NESS. A ness is a headland, as in Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dour is being severe and gloomy, a hard sullen temperament.

clue.text: Duke of a royal house came to a vinous end

definitions.text: Duke of a royal house came to a vinous end

parts.words: Duke of a royal house came to a vinous end
parts.note: a duke of the House of York was said to have been drowned in a butt of Malmsey wine in the Tower

explanation.surface: A royal duke died in a drunken way.
explanation.walkthrough: George, brother of Edward IV, was reputedly drowned in a barrel of Malmsey in 1478, as Shakespeare's Richard III shows.
explanation.definitionFit: George Plantagenet, Duke of Clarence, was executed in 1478, by legend in a butt of wine.

clue.text: Weather conditions etc unsettled round S American capital

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the capital
letters that are unsettled are mixed up

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: Unsettled weather and the rest around a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges ETC into C...TE, and 'round' puts LIMA inside it. 'unsettled' also fits the weather surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual pattern of weather in a region over a long period.

clue.text: Flower rated gold coming first

indicators.note: the gold piece is placed before the other

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to rate someone is to scold them; chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: A flower judged worthy of the gold medal ranks top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rated' looks like 'ranked' but is the old verb rate, scold, so CHID.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic flowering plant prized for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Repository of wealth, like an old city among three

indicators.note: the words go among the letters of the three

parts.note: a trey is a three in dice or cards
as means like
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A store of riches, like an ancient city among three others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts AS + UR inside TREY, the cards-and-dice word for three.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a place where funds or treasure are stored.

clue.text: Early landfall of a deserter from the gunners?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
a rat deserts, as from a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier who deserted from the artillery making early landfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'from' are links. Noah's Ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat, the first land after the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical mountain where the Ark grounded as the flood waters fell.

clue.text: Hung about to chop one old tree

indicators.note: to chop something is to cut it up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man hung around, planning to fell an old tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; 'chop' rearranges I + OLD + TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger idly, staying in a place without purpose.

clue.text: Esteems what may be paid without expense

definitions.meaning: regards highly, holds in high regard

definitions.text: what may be paid without expense
definitions.meaning: one pays one's last ..., honours that cost nothing

explanation.surface: Someone values what can be offered for free.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect is to think highly of; respects are polite regards paid at no cost.

clue.text: Most senior departmental head in processing of steel

indicators.note: the first letter goes into the rearranged metal
the steel is processed, its letters reworked into a new order
the head of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The most senior head of department handles steel production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing of' rearranges STEEL into ELEST, and 'in' places D, the head of 'departmental', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest child of a family, highest in age.
